title: Choose the visual world for ReadAIness
question: The roll assigned the Audit Working Paper. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Audit Working Paper
options.lineage: Auditors' working papers and assurance opinions
options.thesis: Readiness reviewed the way auditors sign off: every figure tickmarked back to its source, every opinion qualified or clean.
options.viewport: Deep working-paper-green side rail with releases; main area opens on the recommendation as an opinion line (Go / Conditional / No-Go), then a dense gate table where each row's evidence carries a blue tickmark keyed to a legend: agreed to source, AI-quoted, signed off, no evidence.
options.risk: Can tip into accounting-software dullness if the tickmarks are timid or the green rail is desaturated.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it cancels: overridden recommendations and superseded checks stay visible, struck through, never deleted.
Readiness history is drawn at one fixed scale per check, so successive checks compare directly.
Every gate keeps fixed furniture (owner, kind, blocking) in the same columns across every release.
Metric values, targets and evidence references are set in tabular mono columns at true data density.

options.label: Launch Poll
options.lineage: 1970s space-agency graphics standards and the launch director's go/no-go poll
options.thesis: Every gate is a station answering the poll; the release launches only when the loop comes back all Go.
options.viewport: White ground on a strict grid; the gates listed as stations in poll order, each answering GO / NO-GO / STANDBY down one column, with the overall call at the top.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of 'go/no-go'; many runs land here, and it can read as space-themed costume.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Only the next decision, signed loud: one band says what blocks the release and who must act.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band carrying the single next decision (e.g. 'Product Owner sign-off · due before Nov 14'), over a plain gate table.
options.case: Strong on clarity in a war room; weaker on identification, since TPMs read reports, not concourses.
options.risk: Yellow reserved for one job can shout over state colours.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: A near-monochrome tool where every claim sits next to its proof.
options.viewport: Neutral shell, recommendation card, gate list with evidence beside each claim.
options.case: Reads instantly as a pro tool (product clarity); loses identification, since it could be any SaaS.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from Linear or Vercel clones.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each check as a coupon that stamps validated, used or void.
options.viewport: A coupon book of checks per release.
options.case: Fuses as a costume; neither audience thinks in tickets.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A release followed through its readiness stages like a plant through seasons.
options.viewport: Five aligned plates per release stage.
options.case: No audience identification and weak clarity.
options.kept: Fixed-scale registration so stages compare directly.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Gates as a ranked roster with fixed personal furniture.
options.case: Undermines the gravity of a go/no-go.
options.kept: Fixed furniture in fixed positions for every entry.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: Readiness as a strobing data field.
options.viewport: A barcode field of gate results.
options.case: Spectacle over decision; loses both axes.
options.kept: Tabular mono figures at true data density.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean neutral dashboard like Linear, Vercel or Datadog, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of releases, status card, gate table, memo panel.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
